subject: Some Interactions between Nimble and R not working in parallel

messages.author: 63cc02caac0434cf
messages.subject: Some Interactions between Nimble and R not working in parallel
parts:
Hi, 

I usually run my nimble models in parallel using the doparallel package and foreach. Typically, this works quite well and since I often run 3 chains it results in a speedup of between 2-3 times. However, as I have started to code more complex models I have run into issues running in parallel. For some reason there are certain interactions between R and Nimble that do not work properly in parallel and I do not understand why.

The main example I have involves removing and adding samplers to several nodes. I use the following for loop which works when not in parallel. 

for(loc in 1:160){
  
dq <- !mainmodel$isData(paste0("S[",loc,", ]"))
mainmodelConf$removeSampler(paste0("S[",loc,", dq]"))
mainmodelConf$addSampler(target = mainmodel$expandNodeNames(paste0("S[",loc,", dq]")),
                        type = "my_sampler")

}

S is a two dimensional node S[1:160,1:85]. Some of S is data and some needs to be sampled. The idea here is that S[loc,dq] are S nodes in location loc that are not data and need to be sampled. I remove the default nimble sampler and then add my own sampler. This works when not in parallel. 

In parallel however it does not work. dq is created correctly as a logical vector but nimble is unable to understand what S[loc,dq] is and print(mainmodel$expandNodeNames(paste0("S[",loc,", dq]"))) returns an empty vector. 

Anyone understand why some things work when not in parallel but do not work when in parallel and how to fix it?

parts:
Hi Chris, 

I created a very simple example that shows the issue 

library(nimble)
library(parallel)

S <- rep(NA,10)
S[c(2,4,6,8)] <- 0
#some S data and some not

mainCode <- nimbleCode({
  
  for(i in 1:10){
    S[i] ~ dbern(.5)
  }
  
}
)

myData <- list(S=S)
myInits <- list(S=rep(1,10))

mainModel <- nimbleModel(code=mainCode,data = myData,inits = myInits)

mainModel$S

dq <- !mainModel$isData("S[]")
mainModel$expandNodeNames("S[dq]")

#so it works here 

parrallel_nimble <- function(X,data,inits){
  
  library(nimble)
  
  mainCode <- nimbleCode({
    
    for(i in 1:10){
      S[i] ~ dbern(.5)
    }
    
  }
  )
  
  mainModel <- nimbleModel(code=mainCode,data = data,inits = inits)
  
  dq <- !mainModel$isData("S[]")
  
  return(mainModel$expandNodeNames("S[dq]"))
  
}

parrallel_nimble(X=1:3,data=myData,inits=myInits)

#works again 

this_cluster <- makeCluster(3)

fit_par <- parLapply(cl = this_cluster,X = 1:3,
                     fun = parrallel_nimble, 
                     data=myData,inits=myInits)

fit_par[[1]]
#just empty character vector

stopCluster(this_cluster)

messages.author: 5fa2a363d4ddd1d1
messages.subject: Re: Some Interactions between Nimble and R not working in parallel
parts:
Hi Dirk, this looks like an issue that is not directly related to parallelization, as you figured out. 

1) The argument to expandNodeNames should be a character vector that provides a valid node (e.g., "S[3]") or nodes (e.g., "S[2:4]") or a valid variable (e.g. "S"). So in your case "S[dq1]" is not valid because there is no node named "S[dq1]", only nodes named "S[1]", "S[2]", etc. 

Here's what you need to do -- evaluate `dq1` and use the result to create a valid node name:
dq1 <- !Model$isData("S[]")

nodeName <- paste0('S[', dq1, ']')
  return(Model$expandNodeNames(nodeName))

2) It's actually an "accident" that what you tried to do worked in any context. Basically, within our processing when we try to determine the set of nodes
that the user has passed in, we actually allow `dq1` to be evaluated when we should really error out.
In some of your cases, R is able to find `dq1` via R's scoping rules and in other cases it is not. When it can't find `dq1`, it returns the error you see.
So it's not surprising that you encountered this in the context of parallelization, where it becomes more complicated to find R variables.

3) We've encountered this issue in other contexts, but I haven't had the time yet to put in better error trapping such that all cases where you
tried to use "S[dq1]" would error out with an error message that would be easy for you to interpret.

Please try the change above, and if you notice any further parallelization issues, let us know.

-chris

On Saturday, June 27, 2020 at 3:57:56 PM UTC-4, Chris Paciorek wrote:

Hi Dirk, this looks like an issue that is not directly related to parallelization, as you figured out. 

1) The argument to expandNodeNames should be a character vector that provides a valid node (e.g., "S[3]") or nodes (e.g., "S[2:4]") or a valid variable (e.g. "S"). So in your case "S[dq1]" is not valid because there is no node named "S[dq1]", only nodes named "S[1]", "S[2]", etc. 

Here's what you need to do -- evaluate `dq1` and use the result to create a valid node name:

  dq1 <- !Model$isData("S[]")
  nodeName <- paste0('S[', dq1, ']')
  return(Model$expandNodeNames(nodeName))

2) It's actually an "accident" that what you tried to do worked in any context. Basically, within our processing when we try to determine the set of nodes
that the user has passed in, we actually allow `dq1` to be evaluated when we should really error out.
In some of your cases, R is able to find `dq1` via R's scoping rules and in other cases it is not. When it can't find `dq1`, it returns the error you see.
So it's not surprising that you encountered this in the context of parallelization, where it becomes more complicated to find R variables.

3) We've encountered this issue in other contexts, but I haven't had the time yet to put in better error trapping such that all cases where you
tried to use "S[dq1]" would error out with an error message that would be easy for you to interpret.

Please try the change above, and if you notice any further parallelization issues, let us know.

-chris

parts:
Hi Dirk, a few thoughts here:

1) You should definitely switch to
nodeName <- paste0('S[', dq1, ']')

Relying on the current syntax is not guaranteed to work in future versions of nimble.

2) It looks like there are some scoping issues with finding your user-defined sampler. 

a) Please define the sampler within your parallelization function as you are doing for the model, MCMC configuration, etc.

Then add this line within your parallelization function:

assign('my_sampler', my_sampler, envir = .GlobalEnv)

The reason this is needed is that nimble is looking in R's global environment for the user defined sampler, but that sampler is being set up inside the parallelization function. I'm going to file an issue for one of the developers to see if we should modify how user-defined samplers are found. 

b) I don't recommend defining the sampler in your main R session as it's a bit tricky to use clusterExport to get the sampler sent out to the workers because nimbleFunctions are more complicated than regular R objects. But I'll make a note that we should look into how to make this easier.

Chris
